documents.unit: Office of Student Conduct (Dean of Students Office)
documents.title: Know the Code Resources: Faculty and Staff (Artificial Intelligence section)
documents.summary: The Office of Student Conduct's faculty page has a short AI section. It says AI may be permitted, restricted or prohibited by course and tells instructors to state expectations, design assignments that show student process, and not rely on detectors alone. It sets no university-wide rule on what students may do.
documents.stance_why: The AI section says tools "may be permitted, restricted, or prohibited depending on the course, assignment, or instructor expectations" and only "encouraged" faculty to communicate expectations, so it sets no stance of its own and hands the decision to instructors (delegates). It offers no named tiers.

units.why: The sentence says AI tools "may be permitted, restricted, or prohibited depending on the course, assignment, or instructor expectations", so no university-wide default is set and the decision is left to course, assignment or instructor (P04). It describes the range rather than ranking it, hence informs/neutral; the actor is all because it is a general statement.
units.anchor: may be permitted, restricted, or prohibited depending on the course, assignment, or instructor expectations

units.why: "faculty and instructors are encouraged to clearly communicate expectations regarding AI use in their syllabi, assignment instructions, and course discussions" asks instructors to state AI expectations in syllabi (P09, not P04, because it is about communicating, not who decides). "Encouraged" gives should.
units.anchor: faculty and instructors are encouraged to clearly communicate expectations regarding AI use in their syllabi
units.frag_start: As a result, faculty and instructors

units.why: "The use of AI is not inherently academic misconduct" says AI use alone does not make misconduct; whether it does depends on course rules, so it fits P04 (rule set per course) better than P36, which covers classifying misuse as misconduct. It is a definitional statement, hence informs/neutral.
units.anchor: The use of AI is not inherently academic misconduct.

units.why: "concerns arise when AI is used in a manner that violates course expectations, provides unauthorized assistance" names the AI uses that raise potential misconduct, i.e. how unauthorized AI use is treated under integrity processes (P36). It informs, and its unit stance is restrict because it limits AI to what the course authorizes.
units.anchor: concerns arise when AI is used in a manner that violates course expectations

units.why: The same sentence adds that concern arises when AI "replaces the student's own demonstration of learning". This is a separate criterion: AI must not stand in for the student's own thinking (P32, since the point is the student remains the primary doer; P19 is about submitting generated work and is not stated this specifically).
units.anchor: replaces the student's own demonstration of learning

units.why: "rather than relying on AI-detection tools alone" tells faculty not to treat AI detectors as sole evidence, which is P39 (detectors not to be relied upon). "Alone" makes it should-not rather than a ban on detectors.
units.anchor: rather than relying on AI-detection tools alone

units.why: "faculty should focus on course expectations, assignment requirements, the student's work product, and any other relevant information" sets what evidence to weigh when evaluating suspected AI misuse. P40 covers tools and process evidence and P57 covers talking to the student, so neither says this; the evidentiary basis for judging AI concerns is uncovered.
units.anchor: faculty should focus on course expectations, assignment requirements, the student's work product
units.uncovered_note: Prescribes which evidence faculty should weigh (course expectations, assignment requirements, work product, other information) when judging suspected AI misuse.

units.why: "CELT has developed resources that may assist faculty in developing syllabus language, discussing AI use with students, and designing assignments" is the university teaching center offering support for instructors setting their AI policy, which is P63 (support faculty). "may assist" gives informs.
units.anchor: CELT has developed resources that may assist faculty in developing

units.why: "Faculty may also review the Office of Student Conduct's guidance regarding referrals involving suspected unauthorized AI use" points to a procedure for handling unauthorized AI use as a conduct matter (P36). It is permissive ("may") and informational.
units.anchor: regarding referrals involving suspected unauthorized AI use

units.why: "Clearly communicate course and assignment expectations regarding AI use, including whether use is permitted, restricted, or prohibited" is a strategy telling instructors to state expectations (P09). "may wish to consider" frames it as a suggestion, so should.
units.anchor: Clearly communicate course and assignment expectations regarding AI use

units.why: "Discuss appropriate and inappropriate uses of AI within the context of your discipline and course learning objectives" asks instructors to talk through acceptable AI uses with students, an act of communicating expectations; P09 is closest because P44 is about teaching AI as a professional skill, which this does not say.
units.anchor: Discuss appropriate and inappropriate uses of AI within the context of your discipline

units.why: "Design assignments that require students to demonstrate their own learning, reasoning, analysis, and application" asks for assignments redesigned in response to AI, which fits P35 (redesign assignments around AI); it is a suggestion so should.
units.anchor: Design assignments that require students to demonstrate their own learning, reasoning, analysis, and application

units.why: "Consider incorporating drafts, reflections, process documentation, in-class work, presentations" proposes assignment formats that show how students got to the product. P35 fits because it is instructor-side redesign; P26 requires students to submit transcripts or reflections, which is not mandated here.
units.anchor: Consider incorporating drafts, reflections, process documentation, in-class work, presentations

units.why: "Encourage students to seek clarification when they are unsure whether a particular use of AI or another resource is permitted" is the ask-before-using rule (P10). The instructor is addressed and told to encourage it, so should.
units.anchor: Encourage students to seek clarification when they are unsure whether a particular use of AI

units.why: "consider discussing the student's work and process with them as part of gathering relevant information" tells instructors to talk with the student when concerns arise, before any referral, which is P57.
units.anchor: consider discussing the student's work and process with them as part of gathering relevant information

units.why: Online "study, tutoring, answer-sharing, and AI platforms may be used appropriately or inappropriately depending on course expectations and instructor authorization" leaves legitimacy of AI platform use to the course and instructor, so P04. It is explanatory (informs).
units.anchor: may be used appropriately or inappropriately depending on course expectations and instructor authorization

units.why: "Faculty are encouraged to communicate clear expectations regarding the use of these resources in their syllabi, assignments, and course discussions" repeats the syllabus-communication ask for AI and answer-sharing platforms, so P09. It is a distinct passage in a separate section.
units.anchor: may be used appropriately or inappropriately depending on course expectations

units.why: CELT and the Office of Student Conduct "have created ... sample statements regarding the use of artificial intelligence" for syllabi, which is institutional support for faculty writing AI syllabus language (P63).
units.anchor: sample statements regarding the use of artificial intelligence

units.why: The tutorial discussion question "What should a student do when they are unsure whether a resource, an AI tool, or a form of collaboration is allowed?" prompts students to consider asking when unsure about an AI tool (P10). It is a suggested prompt, so should.
units.anchor: What should a student do when they are unsure whether a resource, an AI tool

notes: Single included document; only AI-related passages were coded (AI section, AI mentions in the syllabus-statement and tutorial sections, online platforms section). General academic-misconduct text without AI mention was skipped. One UNCOVERED unit (evidence basis for judging AI concerns).
